primary_sources.observed: Path.resolve() makes a path absolute while resolving symlinks; Path.lstat() inspects a symbolic link rather than its target; Path.is_junction() exists on Windows; Path.is_file(follow_symlinks=False) excludes symlinks in Python 3.13.

os.lstat() and os.stat(..., follow_symlinks=False) do not follow the final symbolic link; on Windows follow_symlinks=False disables name-surrogate reparse points including symlinks and directory junctions.

RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS rejects symbolic links in all path components; this is stronger than O_NOFOLLOW, which only affects the final component. RESOLVE_BENEATH/IN_ROOT provide kernel-enforced confinement for hostile path resolution.
Normal pathname resolution follows symbolic links in intermediate components; openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS can block that resolution.

f2_source_audit.original_finding: FALSIFIED_AS_LINK_FREE_WITNESS: _safe_file() resolved root/raw before candidate.is_symlink(), so an in-root symlink became its target before the link check and could pass as a regular file.
f2_source_audit.repair_assessment: The new lexical component walk rejects Path.is_symlink() before strict resolution and therefore directly addresses both final-component and intermediate-component symlink substitution in a stable static release tree.
f2_source_audit.concurrent_regressions: tests/test_portable_release_static_completeness.py@8b176639958d28b0b3a3a6745e6406f29fe05a6a adds final-link and intermediate-link fail-closed cases.
remaining_boundary: Windows junction/name-surrogate reparse points are not shown rejected by the current lexical Path.is_symlink()-only walk; Path.is_junction()/platform-specific no-follow semantics should be evaluated before claiming cross-platform link-free confinement.

The lexical check followed by later resolve/read is not a race-free hostile-directory primitive. If concurrent attacker mutation is in scope, descriptor-based/kernel-enforced resolution such as Linux openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS plus RESOLVE_BENEATH/IN_ROOT is the stronger model. For a frozen/static CI release tree this may be outside the declared threat model, but that boundary must be explicit.
No target-host/runtime/effect/completion credit follows from this source audit or from repository tests alone.
